lead_with.title: An enzyme toolbox for Domainex chemists
lead_with.text: Domainex sells medicinal and synthetic chemistry. Enzymicals can add **biocatalytic steps** (enantioselective reductions, selective oxidations, late-stage functionalisation) that are hard or slow by classic chemistry, **without Domainex building an enzyme lab**.

lead_with.title: Drug metabolites on demand
lead_with.text: Discovery projects often need **human metabolites** of a candidate for testing and analytics. Enzymatic synthesis can make them selectively; Domainex's bioanalytical team is a natural user (to be confirmed with Andrew).

lead_with.title: A path beyond 10 L
lead_with.text: Domainex's own scale-up stops at **10 L**. When a candidate moves on, Enzymicals can take an enzymatic route from mg to ton, so Domainex keeps its client's project moving.

person.name: Andrew (AJ) Ratcliffe
person.text: **Chief Scientific Officer** at Domainex (company website). Medicinal chemist with **more than 30 years** in drug discovery at **Rhône-Poulenc Rorer, Celltech, UCB, Cellzome, Redx Anti-infectives and Novintum Bioscience**. Led projects that nominated several clinical candidates: two JAK inhibitors (rheumatoid arthritis), a mitochondrial disruptor (oncology) and two VLA4 antagonists (MS), one of which, **CDP323**, reached Phase II. Also worked on PDE4, IMPDH, JNK and PI3Kδ inhibitors (UCB5857 entered the clinic) and DNA gyrase antibacterials with European ENABLE funding. First degree and **PhD at the University of Bath**, NATO/SERC postdoc at **Duke University**; 70+ papers and patents. Joined Domainex in **2019**, promoted to **Head of Chemistry** in Nov 2022, now CSO.

company.text: Domainex (founded 2001 as a spin-out of UCL, Birkbeck and the Institute of Cancer Research) is a Cambridge-based **integrated drug discovery CRO**. Services listed: medicinal, synthetic and analytical chemistry, direct-to-biology, CADD/SBDD, protein production, assay development, biochemistry/enzymology, biophysics, cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography, bioanalytics. Chemistry sits at the **Medicines Research Centre, Chesterford Research Park**; a three-storey **Biology Centre of Excellence** (24,000+ sq ft) opened at Unity Campus, Pampisford in 2024. **CEO: Hayley French, PhD** (since May 2025, ex-CEO of Apitope); former CEO **Eddy Littler** became non-executive Chairman. Other leaders: **Ray Boffey** (CCO), Tom Amies (Finance Director). Domainex won the **King's Award for Enterprise: International Trade 2023** after international revenue grew more than 100% in three years.

financials.text: Private company: no revenue published in the sources checked (UK Companies House accounts **to be confirmed**). Growth signals: 100+ scientists, a new 24,000 sq ft biology building (2024) and international revenue up **more than 100% over three years** (King's Award 2023). A growing CRO is more likely to **add a partner** than build an enzyme platform itself.

industry.title: Biocatalysis moves earlier into discovery
industry.text: Engineered enzymes are no longer only a process-chemistry tool: discovery chemists use them for chiral intermediates, late-stage C–H oxidation and metabolite synthesis.

industry.title: CROs compete on breadth
industry.text: Integrated CROs win projects by offering more under one roof. Partnering for a niche skill like biocatalysis is faster than building it.

industry.title: Greener chemistry from day one
industry.text: Pharma clients increasingly ask for sustainable routes early, so the route chosen in discovery doesn't need a full redesign later.

talking_points: Do any current Domainex chemistry projects struggle with a **chiral centre or a selective oxidation** where an enzyme could help?
How do you produce **drug metabolites** for clients today: in-house synthesis, purchase, or not at all?
What happens to a client's route **after your 10 L scale-up**? Would a hand-over partner for enzymatic steps be useful?
Would a small **feasibility screen on one Domainex compound or intermediate** be easy to set up as a pilot?
Who in your chemistry team would be the right day-to-day contact for a technical exchange?
